previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was readmitted with persistent left-sided abdominal pain following a recent episode of peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis. Despite completing a week of intraperitoneal vancomycin and ceftazidime, her pain did not improve. Admission labs showed elevated peritoneal fluid white blood cells (730), supporting ongoing peritonitis, though cultures remained negative. A CT scan ruled out diverticulitis, showing only changes related to dialysis catheter use. She underwent peritoneal irrigation and continued antibiotics, with subsequent improvement in symptoms and a drop in peritoneal WBC to 14. Fungal and TB studies were negative, and fluconazole was discontinued. Her gastroparesis flared during admission, managed with domperidone and restarted metoclopramide with QTc monitoring. Diabetes was managed with adjusted insulin dosing. She completed a 10-day course of antibiotics and was discharged home with plans for follow-up in gastroenterology and nephrology.
problems: End stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis
Infection and inflammatory reaction due to peritoneal dialysis catheter

infection given hx. Pt was admitted for peritoneal infection in 
___ and discharged on 14 day course of IP vancomcyin and 
ceftazidime ending  ___ but had not been on IP abx since. On 
this admission, peritoneal cultures show NO GROWTH. She was 
afebrile, and her abdominal pain was improving by discharge. Her 
symptoms were likely ___ worsening of gastroparesis and possibly 
viral gastroenteritis rather than infection as PD, urine, and 
blood cultures were all negative and a CXR was reassuring. She 
was very constipated this admission and required an aggressive 
bowel regimen. The importance of minimizing stool burden in 
order to optimize PD was discussed. She was continued on her 
home domperidone (started on ___ while inpatient and was 
dialyzed daily. 

#GASTROPARESIS: chronic issue in the setting of poorly 
controlled diabetes and constipation.  
Restarted her home DOMPERIDONE on ___ with meals, which patient 
brought in from home. Attending note in chart and general order 
for med. She received daily EKGs to monitor QT prolongation ___ 
domperidone. Bowel meds doubled, and enemas and lactulose added 
with moderate success. 

#Vaginal discharge/burning/pain: pt reported worsening of these 
symptoms over the past month, consistent with prior yeast 
infections. She endorsed white discharge, with no odor. She was 
treated on 3 separate occasions with fluconazole PO 150mg since 
early ___ without resolution of sxs. Mild erythema and white 
d/c were noted on pelvic exam, which was performed to further 
evaluate for cervical and adnexal tenderness given presenting 
symptoms. The findings on exam were most consistent with 
candidate infection and she was given fluconazole 150mg x1.  
Laboratory results returning after discharge showed that urine 
GC/chlamydia was negative. and a swab was indeterminate for BV 
and negative for yeast. Given indeterminate BV result, if 
symptoms persist, treatment for BV may be warranted. 

#Toe infection: Likely paronychia. One month duration ___ 
stubbing toe walking on beach. Podiatry attempted to treat as 
outpatient with lancing and nail trimming and 10 day course of 
cephalexin. Pt reported no improvement in toe with treatment. No 
sign of lymphatic spread. It is unlikely, given the mild 
appearance and duration of stable symptoms, that this is the 
cause of her systemic complaints. Podiatry was consulted and 
trimmed nail, noting scant purulent discharge and recommended 
abx, which were initiated. PO abx d/c'd in favor of topical 
given pt's multiple QT prolonging agents and relatively benign 
appearance of toe. Plain films of right foot neg for fx or signs 
of osteomyelitis. 

# ESRD on PD: Renal notified of pt and consulted on admission. 
Patient encouraged  continue to work on clearing stool burden. 
Daily PD while inpatient. 

#T1DM: Poorly controlled with multiple complications. Followed 
by ___. Blood glucose 178 on admission. Maintained on Lantus 
15U at bedtime, added 6U at BF. Humalog 3U with B,L,D,N unless 
full tray. ISS.

Indeterminate. Altered vaginal flora that does not meet criteria for diagnosis of bacterial vaginosis. If signs and/or symptoms persist, repeat testing may be warranted.  Interpretive criteria have only been established for pre-menopausal women and post-menopausal women on hormone replacement therapy. As low estrogen levels alter vaginal flora, results should be interpreted with caution in post-menopausal women. Refer to the on line laboratory manual.  Note, neither lactobacilli nor Gardnerella/Bacteroides/Mobiluncus morphotypes observed. The absence of these morphotypes likely represents normal flora in post-menopausal women.
